newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Doctors tell Yeltsin to skip radio address.
newsitem.headline: Doctors tell Yeltsin to skip radio address.

text.p: Doctors have told Russian President Boris Yeltsin not to give his traditional radio address to the nation this week because of his preparations for heart surgery, Interfax news agency said on Thursday.
Interfax quoted the presidential press office as saying the address had been postponed in line with a decision to cancel all Yeltsin's working meetings this week to undergo health tests.

Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, announced the decision to cancel Yeltsin's meetings earlier this week, saying the president had begun the last stage of preparations for the bypass operation to improve blood supply to his heart.
U.S. cardiologist Michael DeBakey, a consultant to the Russian doctors who are due to operate on the 65-year-old president, has made clear that the operation could go ahead as early as next week.
The final date of the operation is likely to be decided when DeBakey meets his Russian colleagues in Moscow on Monday.

Heart trouble has kept Yeltsin away from his Kremlin office since he was re-elected in July. Yeltsin, who is currently at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow, announced on September 5 that he would need an operation .
